---
title: "Task 2: Do Bigrams Capture Additional Information?"
author: Daniel Nickolov
output: pdf_document
---

## Objectives

* Perform a secondary tokenization of the data to obtain bigrams
* Fit a logistic principal component regression model to the word-tokenized data

## Setup

```{r setup}
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = normalizePath(".."))

library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(tokenizers)
library(textstem)
library(stopwords)

source("../scripts/preprocessing.R")
load("../data/claims-clean-example.RData") # I had too many memory issues so I'm using the example cleaned data

claims_df <- claims_clean %>%
  filter(bclass %in% c("Relevant claim content", "N/A: No relevant content.")) %>%
  mutate(
    doc_id = row_number(),
    claim_target = factor(if_else(bclass == "Relevant claim content", 1, 0), levels = c("1", "0")) # making into binary for regression purposes
  ) %>%
  select(doc_id, text_clean, claim_target)
```

# Tokenization

## Fitting to Word-Tokenized Data (Unigrams)

```{r}
set.seed(111126)
unigram_recipe <- recipe(claim_target ~ text_clean + doc_id, data = claims_df) %>%
  update_role(doc_id, new_role = "ID") %>%
  step_tokenize(text_clean, token = "words") %>%
  step_stopwords(text_clean) %>%
  step_tokenfilter(text_clean, max_tokens = 1000) %>%
  step_tf(text_clean) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_pca(all_predictors(), num_comp = 20, prefix = "unigram_PC")

unigram_prep <- prep(unigram_recipe)
unigram_pcs <- bake(unigram_prep, new_data = NULL)

fit_unigram <- glm(claim_target ~ . - doc_id, data = unigram_pcs, family = binomial)
claims_df$log_odds_unigram <- predict(fit_unigram, newdata = unigram_pcs, type = "link")
```

## Fitting Bigrams

```{r}
set.seed(111126)
bigram_recipe <- recipe(~ text_clean + doc_id, data = claims_df) %>%
  update_role(doc_id, new_role = "ID") %>%
  step_tokenize(text_clean, token = "ngrams", options = list(n = 2)) %>%
  step_stopwords(text_clean) %>%
  step_tokenfilter(text_clean, max_tokens = 1000) %>%
  step_tf(text_clean) %>%
  step_normalize(all_predictors()) %>%
  step_pca(all_predictors(), num_comp = 10, prefix = "bigram_PC") # K = 10 bigram principle components

bigram_prep <- prep(bigram_recipe)
bigram_pcs <- bake(bigram_prep, new_data = NULL)
```

Now, we can stack the unigram and bigram PCs into one model and run an ANOVA test to determine if the bigrams do capture additional information.

## Setup

```{r}
stacked_df <- claims_df %>%
  select(doc_id, claim_target, log_odds_unigram) %>%
  inner_join(bigram_pcs, by = "doc_id") %>%
  select(-doc_id)

fit_base <- glm(claim_target ~ log_odds_unigram, data = stacked_df, family = binomial)
fit_stacked <- glm(claim_target ~ ., data = stacked_df, family = binomial)
```

## Running the ANOVA

```{r}
lrt_result <- anova(fit_base, fit_stacked, test = "Chisq")
print(lrt_result)
```
Running the test, we get a $p\text{-value}$ of `r lrt_result$Pr(>Chi)[[2]]`, which is well above a standard level of significance of $\alpha=0.05$, meaning that when comparing unigram-tokenized data to bigram-tokenized data in this dataset, there isn't a significant difference in the information captured about a page.
